notes.text: The Bavli chain has Rabbi Yose bar Chanina from Rav Huna. In Rosh the first occurrence reads Rabbi Yitzchak but the lemma omits Huna. A later Rosh quotation gives the full Yitzchak–Huna chain. Check the exact Rif before sealing.
The checked text gives plain Rabbi Yose as he transmits Resh Lakish after Ravin reports. Heilprin’s patronymic expansion is expressly conjectural.
The rabbis of Caesarea explicitly quote Yose son of Chanina on permission in the case of a dangerous robber.
The act of derision is explicitly shown in the preceding Shabbat 62b passage. A separate Yerushalmi has Abbahu transmit in Yose’s name.
The exact transmission occurs on the Shabbat labors and in the Jerusalem laws of the sabbatical year.
The local discussion and Nazir put Yose as the one objecting to Rav Acha. The catalogue’s terse wording is ambiguous by itself. Align the grammatical subject with its explicit backward pointer.
The local quotation names the great man as Yose. The checked Bavli says Rav Assi.
The Bavli quotes Yose reporting Rav Huna. The narrator’s question likewise asks how Yose could cite Huna. The English can make this direction clear while retaining its title convention.
Rif and Rosh’s later quotation attest Yitzchak followed by Huna. Rosh’s earlier lemma gives Yitzchak without Huna. The local version difference is consequential.
Both Jerusalem witnesses give R. Zerikan quoting Yose about the leaven measures.
The Jerusalem Gittin story gives this transmission about a widow, independently of the next attribution in that segment.
The Jerusalem Sheviit passage identifies Oshaya’s father, but its compact chain includes Yaakov bar Acha. Preserve the grouping as transmitted.
The Jerusalem Berakhot gives the exact report about starting the reader’s prayer again after a mistake.
The named transmission and its ruling on decayed stolen produce are in the Jerusalem chapter at 9:3:2.
Terumot explicitly names Yudan as Yose’s sister’s son and also records his transmission.
The related entry itself reports the unsuccessful lookup and proposes Yehudah in its place. Both names and the uncertainty remain distinct.
Both Jerusalem passages list Rabbi Yonah and Yose Gelilaya quoting Yose son of Chanina.
The Bavli gives Yose bar Chanina’s anger at Gelilaya. The two Jerusalem parallels and adjacent Heilprin entry explicitly make Gelilaya the transmitter in Chanina’s name.
The pointer in this article leads to the episode about the sons, where Yose HaKohen reports about Yose bar Chanina through Abba HaKohen. It does not present a direct quotation from the bereaved sage.
The cited previous entry quotes the exact Jerusalem Shabbat transmission. A neighboring variant is discussed in the related batch.
The Jerusalem Sheviit names Yaakov with Hezekiah in the comparison of measures.
Sukkah explicitly has Yose ben Chanina transmit Menachem’s explanation about making the event public.
The Bavli has Puga the attendant. The internal article preserves both Puga and Suga as reported readings. Keep Suga in the main text with the checked variant named.
The sacrifice ruling is explicitly transmitted by Mar Ukva bar Chama.
The Jerusalem Shekalim gives two precise attributions from Krispa to Yose about meat found in public.
The received sending formula occurs in the discussion of the arranged text of the Mishnah.
The checked text gives plain Rabbi Yose as he transmits Resh Lakish after Ravin reports. Heilprin’s patronymic expansion is expressly conjectural.
Gittin gives the same proposed direction of attribution. The exact Keritot occurrence preserves a bare name, so the parallel is evidence for the narrator’s reasoning, not for silently expanding it.
Both Jerusalem Chagigah passages attest this transmission concerning festival offerings.
The rabbis of Caesarea explicitly quote Yose son of Chanina on permission in the case of a dangerous robber.
The Yerushalmi explicitly gives this transmission with the Nasseh spelling, about accepting a commitment to pay.
The exact named transmission occurs in the preceding Yom HaKippurim source, with a bracketed reading for Yose.
The catalogue juxtaposes both names without a verb, linkage or locator. Retain both as bare names.
Bare juxtaposition does not assert studenthood. The earlier Yoma witness explicitly neighbors the name Zeora bar Chama and Yose in a variant attribution.

Keep the unqualified entries as bare forms. A specific Yerushalmi ruling names Chalfai together with Yose, and the Megillah chain names Chelbo upstream. These attestations do not regularize the list into a single class of relations.
Keep this as a bare item. Shekalim records him discussing separate dicta involving Yose bar Chanina.
Both are bare forms with no transmission direction or locator.
The catalogue supplies the patronymic only and makes no additional relationship to Yose here.
Preserve the bare conjunction and name without an inferred relationship.
